# Dialog

The dialog panel itself: header (title, optional description, header actions, close button, or custom header / tabs), scrolling body, and optional footer slots. Sizes from the screen grid (`4-col · 6-col · 8-col · 10-col`) and renders inline with no Blanket and no modal behavior. For a blocking overlay dialog with Blanket, portal, focus trap, Escape and scroll lock, use the `Modal` template from `@/templates`.

Also asked as: dialog panel, dialog layout.

**Import:** `import { Dialog } from '@/components';`

**Used in:** Modal (`ds guide modal`)

**Governed by:** Errors (`ds guide errors`); Forms (`ds guide forms`); Notifications (`ds guide notifications`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/Dialog/Dialog.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/Dialog/Dialog.stories.jsx` — Width4Col, Width6Col, Width8Col, Width10Col, HeightHug, HeightFill, HeaderOptions, WithoutCloseButton, Tabs, Loading, Content, Layout, Interactive, Overview, FooterLayouts, SizeToContent, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused

## Usage

Use `Dialog` as the panel inside the Modal template, or when a docs illustration or mockup draws the dialog panel inline with no Blanket and no modal behavior. For a working overlay over the page (Blanket, portal, focus trap, Escape and scroll lock), use the `Modal` template from `@/templates`.

The footer runs on `FooterActions`: pass `primaryButton` and `secondaryButton`
as objects for a `50/50` pair (or `primaryButton` alone for the right half), or
pass `footer` with `<FooterActions>` for three actions or a leading action
(a `danger` side action or a link).

### Width guidance

`width` takes a step of `DIALOG_WIDTHS` (4-col · 6-col · 8-col · 10-col): that
many columns of the screen grid plus the dialog pad.

| Width | When to use | `DIALOG_WIDTH_PX` at 768 · 1024 · 1280 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4-col | A compact confirmation. | 269 · 355 · 440 |
| 6-col | A confirmation or a short question. | 392 · 520 · 648 |
| 8-col | A short form. | 515 · 685 · 856 |
| 10-col | A table or an editor. | 637 · 851 · 1064 |

`Dialog` draws `--ds-surface-material-overlay` and a `--ds-border-material` edge with `--dialog-shadow` (`--ds-shadow-blocking`) in every width. A `Select` list opened inside it keeps `--ds-shadow-overlay`.

The width grows with the screen, never shrinks, and ignores the Sidebar. The
height hugs its content up to the cap (`--dialog-max-height`);
`height="fill"` sits at that cap.

## Alternatives

- For a blocking overlay over the page with Blanket, focus trap, Escape and scroll lock, use `Modal` (`@/templates`).
- For a message the person only reads, use `SectionMessage` in the page or `Flag` at the screen corner.
- For a task that keeps the page in view, use `Panel`, floating: a row's details, filters, a short edit.
- For a small aside anchored to a control, use `Popup`.
- For a list of actions or a value to pick, use `DropdownMenu` or `Select`.

## Best practices

### Size the Dialog to its content with a step of `DIALOG_WIDTHS`. {#size-the-dialog-to-its-content-with-a-step-of-dialogwidths}

A short confirmation takes `6-col`, a short form `8-col`, a table or an editor
`10-col`. A step grows with the screen; a fixed number keeps one size on every
screen.

Do: The narrowest step for a short question.

Don't: The widest step around one sentence.

### Keep Close on a Dialog unless the person has to answer it. {#keep-close-on-a-dialog-unless-the-person-has-to-answer-it}

An informational `Dialog` keeps its close button; `showCloseButton={false}` is
for a decision that has to be answered from the footer.

Do: Close stays on an informational dialog.
Don't: No way out of an informational dialog.

### Add `dividers` when the Dialog body scrolls. {#add-dividers-when-the-dialog-body-scrolls}

The rules mark where the header and footer stay put while the body scrolls; a
short body reads cleaner without them.

Do: Dividers around a scrolling body.
Don't: Dividers around a short body.

### Give the Dialog footer a button. {#give-the-dialog-footer-a-button}

`showBottomButtons` defaults to true, and the footer renders only when
`primaryButton`, `secondaryButton` or `footer` is given; describe the actions as
objects and the component renders the `FooterActions` pair.

Do: Pass `primaryButton` or `footer` when the dialog asks for a decision.

Don't: Leave a confirm dialog with no footer action.

### Use `Modal` from `@/templates` when a task needs a Blanket and focus trap. {#use-modal-from-templates-when-a-task-needs-a-blanket-and-focus-trap}

`Dialog` draws the panel inline; `Modal` places it on a Blanket with Base UI
focus management, Escape dismissal and scroll lock.

Do: Use `Modal` for live overlay confirmations and short forms.

Don't: Render a bare `Dialog` over page content on your own.

## Accessibility

- **The close button is labeled `Close`**, hard-coded. Its icon is
  `aria-hidden`. `showCloseButton={false}` removes it.
- **The title is the dialog's h1 and its accessible name**, through
  `aria-labelledby`: the panel reads as its own page. The `description`
  describes it, through `aria-describedby`. A `Dialog` with no title takes
  `ariaLabel`.
- **A body that scrolls is focusable.** Once the content runs past the cap, the
  body gets `tabIndex={0}` so a keyboard user can scroll it.
- **Loading is announced as busy.** `loading` sets `aria-busy` on the body while
  the skeleton bars stand in for it.
- **`Dialog` has no Blanket, focus trap or Escape handling.** Use
  Modal for live blocking dialogs over
  the page.

## Related

- `Modal` template: places `Dialog` on a Blanket with portal, focus trap, Escape and scroll lock.
- `FooterActions`: use when placing three actions or a leading action across the Dialog's four-track footer slot.
- Templates: use when choosing between a Modal and a full page; its Usage section weighs the two.

Same group: `Banner` · `EmptyState` · `Flag` · `InlineMessage` · `NotificationItem` · `SectionMessage` · `Spotlight`

## Parts

1. **Header.** Title, optional description, header actions and the close button, or a custom `header` and optional `tabs`.
2. **Body.** Text, tabs panel, or any content; scrolls when it overflows.
3. **Footer.** Appears only when a button or `footer` is given: `FooterActions` divides the width inside container padding into four equal tracks.
4. **Dividers.** Optional rules under the header and over the footer.

The tokens each part draws are read from `Dialog.scss` and listed under Tokens
touched in the Harness tab.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Drawn inline with the title naming the dialog. |
| Hovered | The close button takes the subtle hovered step. |
| Pressed | The close button takes the subtle pressed step. |
| Focused | The close button shows the focus ring. |
| Disabled | The dialog has no disabled state; disable a footer button instead. |
| Loading | The body shows a skeleton and sets `aria-busy`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Title the Dialog with the action or decision: "Delete account?". | Use a vague title such as "Warning". |
| Say what happens and whether it can be undone. | Hide the consequence in the body. |
| Label buttons with verbs that match the title: "Delete recording", "Archive instead". | Use "Cancel", "Yes" or "No" in a Dialog footer. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | The `id` attribute of the dialog panel. |
| `title` | node | — | The dialog's h1, and its accessible name. |
| `description` | node | — | A line under the title, read as the dialog's description. |
| `ariaLabel` | string | — | The dialog's accessible name when it has no visible `title` or uses a custom `header`. |
| `header` | node | — | Custom header slot replacing the title row (title and close button), so the caller owns both and names the dialog with `ariaLabel`. |
| `headerActions` | node | — | Icon buttons in the header, before the close button. |
| `showCloseButton` | bool | — | The header's close button. Off for a dialog that has to be answered. |
| `tabs` | arrayOf | — | Tab group under the title (`{ key, label, content, disabled? }`). The body becomes the tab panel and shows the selected tab's `content`. |
| `activeTab` | string or number | — | Selected tab's key when controlled; update from `onTabChange`. |
| `defaultActiveTab` | string or number | — | Initial tab key when uncontrolled; defaults to the first enabled tab. |
| `onTabChange` | func | — | Called with the key of the selected tab. |
| `body` | string or node | — | The main content of the dialog. A string is drawn as body text; a node is drawn as given. `children` is rendered after it. |
| `height` | enum | — | `hug` grows with the content to the cap and then scrolls its body; `fill` sits at that cap. |
| `showBottomButtons` | bool | — | Show the footer: `footer`, or the secondary and primary buttons. |
| `footer` | node | — | Custom footer content in place of the built-in pair, such as a three-button or leading-text FooterActions layout. |
| `primaryButton` | buttonShape | — | The confirming footer button, drawn on the right. Takes `text` (default "Confirm"), `onClick`, `appearance` (default `primary`), `spacing` and `icon`. |
| `secondaryButton` | buttonShape | — | The secondary footer button, drawn in the left half when a primary button is also given. Takes `text` (default "Discard"), `onClick`, `appearance` (default `default`), `spacing` and `icon`. |
| `dividers` | bool | — | A rule under the header and over the footer. |
| `loading` | bool | — | Skeleton bars in place of the body while its content loads. |
| `onClose` | func | — | Called when the close button is clicked. |
| `width` | enum or number or string | — | `4-col` · `6-col` · `8-col` · `10-col`: 4 · 6 · 8 · 10 columns of the screen grid plus the dialog pad. Grows with the screen, never shrinks, ignores the sidebar. A number or a length sets a fixed width. |
| `className` | string | — | Extra class names added to the dialog panel beside the component's own. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline styles for the dialog panel. A fixed `width` is applied after them. |
| `children` | node | — | More content rendered in the body after `body`, for composing the dialog contents directly. |
